A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Attention as a Hypernetwork, with matching authors, core derivations, methods, and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original fuzzy-logic and SRAVEN experiments, latent-code analyses, model ablations, and WikiText-103 language-modeling results.

after.justification: v3 retains original reasoning-task experiments and adds decoding, sensitivity, and architectural analyses, together with C4 language-modeling results.

M1.justification: Standard HYLA's equations and Algorithm 2 remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 introduces HYLA+ with an additional hypernetwork-generated hidden layer and nonlinearity, formally defined in Equation 10. This is a limited architectural extension studied through ablation.

E1.justification: The language-modeling evaluation replaces WikiText-103 with C4. SRAVEN evaluation also expands from the standard four-feature setting to five and six features in Figure 5D, increasing the number of rules that must be resolved together. Fuzzy-logic testing on unknown terms was already reported in v1 and is not new coverage.

E2.justification: The principal softmax-attention and linear-attention comparators remain. Table A1 adds controls using linear attention with RMSHead and a nonlinear value network, HYLA with softmax normalization, and deeper HYLA; it also includes standard softmax results. The earlier HYLA linear rows are retained under names describing removal of the nonlinearity.

E3.justification: The replacement language experiment changes from a reported 2M-parameter model and context-length sweep to 50M-parameter models trained for 130B tokens. Appendix C changes its layer count, dimensions, batch size, positional encoding, vocabulary, and hyperparameter search settings. New analyses introduce logistic-regression decoding evaluated on unseen compositions and attention-head sweeps; these are added protocols rather than changes to the retained benchmark results.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative latent-code decoding on both reasoning tasks, SRAVEN head-count and feature-count sensitivity tests, and cosine-similarity analysis of rule codes. Appendix A expands architectural controls and supplies a quantitative plot for the previously described unknown-term failure. Conversely, the WikiText-103 context-length sensitivity study is removed.

E5.justification: Table A1 retains standard errors over three seeds, and Table A2 retains the same Monte Carlo uncertainty reporting. However, language-modeling presentation changes from error-barred WikiText-103 results in v1 Figure A2 to C4 training curves without reported uncertainty in v3 Figure 6. This establishes a reporting change, not a reduction in run counts.

E6.justification: Original Table A1 values are retained, including HYLA's reported fuzzy-logic R2 of 81.13 ± 7.77 and SRAVEN accuracy of 69.13 ± 1.90. New rows include deeper HYLA at 87.65 ± 4.54 and 66.59 ± 0.08, respectively. v3 also adds decoding and sensitivity results and replaces WikiText-103 perplexities with C4 learning curves; the latter do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.

T1.justification: The central attention decomposition and standard HYLA derivation remain intact. v3 adds the mathematical definition of deeper HYLA in Equation 10, corrects the fuzzy-term count from 2^N to 2^L, and removes the assertion that HYLA preserves recurrent, linear-time inference. The earlier granularity discussion survives in prose in Section 7.

C1.justification: The principal claims about the hypernetwork decomposition, HYLA, compositional generalization, and SRAVEN are retained. The revised abstract more explicitly claims that training-acquired latent codes are reused on unseen compositions, while the contribution list adds parametrically controlled SRAVEN difficulty and frames HYLA more explicitly as a test of the proposed mechanism.

C2.justification: v3 changes the explanation of HYLA's gains from primarily nonlinearity to the combination of nonlinearity and RMSHead. It adds interpretations involving shared codes for related rules, head-count dependence, and initialization scale explaining poor softmax-normalized HYLA performance. The language-modeling discussion now argues practical relevance from C4 results, while the earlier limitation discussing softmax-induced interactions between latent codes is removed.

D1.justification: The language-modeling reproduction recipe is substantially replaced: Appendix C documents NanoDo tokenization with a 32,000-token vocabulary instead of 6,144, rotary positional encodings, and revised architecture and optimization settings. Appendix D adds NanoDo and reports 16 Cloud TPU v5e devices, 72–100 hours per run, and approximately 163 TPU-days instead of the earlier GPU-based WikiText estimates. The code-access URL remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Zoology, In-Context Learning and Induction Heads, RoFormer, and NanoDo, supporting the revised language-modeling discussion and implementation. It removes several linear-time-attention references and references associated with the discarded WikiText setup. The central positioning relative to fast-weight programmers, compositionality, and Raven benchmarks remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution list are substantially rewritten, the granularity subsection is incorporated into the discussion, and language modeling becomes a main-text section. SRAVEN and appendix subsections are reorganized, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed while reproducibility and acknowledgement statements are added. These changes substantially revise the narrative structure beyond introducing new results.

P2.justification: Figures 2 and 5 are substantially redesigned to integrate new analyses and selected latent visualizations, with existing all-layer plots retained in the appendix. The 16-layer visualization changes from a narrow vertical strip to readable grids. Table A1 merges duplicated method columns into a consolidated comparison, and the task-count figures are combined into a multipanel display.

improvement.justification: v1 supports latent-code structure mainly through t-SNE visualizations; v3 adds decoding on unseen compositions and targeted architectural and sensitivity controls. These substantially strengthen the empirical basis of the central interpretation, while redesigned figures improve scrutiny. Tradeoffs remain: the WikiText context-length study disappears, C4 curves lack uncertainty reporting, and the claim that both HYLA components are required is too broad for Table A1's fuzzy-logic results. Nevertheless, the added diagnostic evidence provides a substantial overall improvement without establishing causal code reuse.
